title: Prove the reply on the real engine in the hidden rig

proofs.pass: mutant [a-z-]+: RED as it must be
selftest: model all pass, mutant model red

mutants.find: let ["message", id, "thread_headers"] = p[..] else { return None };

notes: Built by lane gap-moved-slice, run on a build by the lead (nothing here was compiled or run: only `python3 checks/realcore-check.py --selftest` and `python3 checks/realcore_mailfake.py --selftest`). Proof 0 is the slice-5 reply (a mail the server still holds). Proof 1, run `python3 checks/realcore-check.py <bundle> --slice-moved` (hidden, real core): checks/realcore-check.py main_slice_moved, judge_moved, drive_moved, selftest_moved; it prints one line per case, `PASS|FAIL|NOT JUDGED <case> <detail>`, and ends `N checks, F failed, U not judged`; the passing lines are `PASS       a-mail-moved-away-on-the-server-leaves-the-apps-inbox  ...` and `PASS       a-reply-to-a-stored-mail-whose-server-copy-moved-is-queued-with-in-reply-to-and-references  ...` (the app-wide `no-outbound-refused` line follows). Proof 2 is the same with `--mutant`: WHOOSH_CORE_MUTANT=reply-ignores-store (engine rust_core.rs Mutant::ReplyIgnoresStore, honoured by outbox adapters/reply/mod.rs `stored`) and it prints `mutant reply-ignores-store: RED as it must be (...)` when the reply case went red. The fake (checks/realcore_mailfake.py): `plain=True` (no change list: CONDSTORE/QRESYNC commands are recorded and refused), `refs=True` (a References chain on each mail), `move_away(mail, uid, to_folder, quiet)` and `announce(mail)`. The engine read the check waits on: `core state message/<id>/thread_headers` (core/crates/engine/src/state_headers.rs, one dispatch line in rust_core.rs state()), the stored Message-ID and References as JSON. DEVIATION from the first gap text: the two cases move two different mails. The sync deletes a vanished mail's row (core/crates/engine/src/sync.rs:347 delete_messages), so once the app has been told mail 2 left, the store holds nothing to reply from; the reply therefore answers mail 1, which the server moves without telling the app (the fake is quiet until `wake`), the app's own reader still showing it: the owner's stale-mail case. Broken copies: proof 2 for the reply case (hook), mutants[0] for the reply case (source), mutants[1] for the inbox case (the sync keeps the vanished row). Unverified until the lead runs it: that J then Enter reaches mail 1, that the engine stores the headers before the move, and what the thread view does with a mail the server moved.
